hypothesis: A one-dimensional cellular automaton of radius r can enlarge the region of non-background cells by at most 2r cells per step (light-cone bound), whereas a neighbour-independent substitution system can multiply its number of elements by a constant factor lambda > 1 per step. Hence for every substitution system with lambda > 1, any emulation in which each element occupies at least one cell needs a number of cellular-automaton steps per substitution step that grows without bound (at least (L_t - L_{t-1})/2r for step t), while Turing machines can be emulated one step per cellular-automaton step.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. (A) Light-cone bound: for all 128 elementary rules with quiescent background (000 -> 0), 10 random finite seeds of 20 cells each, 300 steps on a lattice wide enough never to reach the edge, the width of the non-zero region (rightmost minus leftmost black cell plus one) never increases by more than 2 in one step; likewise never by more than 4 for 50 random radius-2 two-colour rules with quiescent background (seeds 0-49), 5 seeds each, 200 steps. (B) Multiplicative growth: among all 225 two-colour neighbour-independent substitution systems with blocks of length 0-3, at least 50% have Perron root lambda > 1 of their 2x2 growth matrix, and for every system the lengths L_t for t <= 12 from a single black cell equal the matrix prediction exactly. (C) Growing cost: for every system with lambda > 1, the number of radius-1 cellular-automaton steps needed to contain L_12 cells starting from L_0 = 1, ceil((L_12 - L_0)/2), exceeds 12 (more than one CA step per substitution step on average), and the per-step requirement c_t = ceil((L_t - L_{t-1})/2) at t = 12 is at least 4 times c_t at t = 4 (progressively more steps). (D) Contrast with Turing machines: a radius-1 cellular automaton with k(s+1) colours (cell = tape colour x {no head, head state}) built mechanically from the Turing-machine rule reproduces the tape and head of 20 random 2-colour, 2-4-state Turing machines exactly at every one of 200 steps. 'Supports' requires A-D.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if A is violated for any rule, seed and step (the fixed-growth premise is false), or if any system with lambda > 1 has ceil((L_12 - L_0)/2) <= 12 (one CA step per substitution step is not excluded by the bound), or if D fails for any machine (Turing machines cannot be emulated step for step either, so the contrast is false). Other combinations are 'mixed'.
interpretation: The claim is a counting argument. Its premise (fixed growth per CA step) is checked exhaustively over the elementary rules and on random larger-radius rules; the second premise (multiplicative growth of substitution systems) is checked over the complete family of two-colour systems with blocks of length 0-3 (NKS p. 82-83 convention: every element is replaced by the block for its colour; an empty block deletes the element); the conclusion is quantified as the minimal number of CA steps per substitution step under the only assumption that each element occupies at least one cell of the pattern (the encoding Wolfram's figures use; a compressed encoding would fall outside the claim's 'size of a pattern' reasoning). The clause 'unlike ... Turing machines' is checked by an explicit one-step-per-step construction (NKS p. 657). Computational; all programs generated by analysis.py.

datasets.name: Elementary and radius-2 cellular automata, two-colour substitution systems, random Turing machines (generated by analysis.py)

generator.program_family: A: 128 ECA rules with bit 0 = 0 (Wolfram code); 50 radius-2 rules with random 32-bit tables and table[0] = 0; B/C: 225 substitution systems (block for white, block for black) over the 15 binary blocks of length 0-3; D: 20 random 2-colour Turing machines with 2-4 states
generator.initial_conditions: A: random 20-cell seeds (numpy default_rng seeds 0-9 / 0-4) centred on a zero lattice of width 20 + 2*2r*steps + 4; B/C: single black cell; D: random 40-cell tape, head at the centre, state 0
generator.steps: A: 300 (ECA), 200 (radius 2); B/C: 12 substitution steps; D: 200 TM steps = 200 CA steps

datasets.role: program families whose growth and emulation properties are measured
